findings.statement: CXCR2 leads the convergence ranking: strongly up in biopsies (meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814]), Open Targets overall association [gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5345], tractable as small molecule and antibody, with clinical CXCR2 antagonists (reparixin Phase 3, navarixin, ladarixin, danirixin, SX-682 Phase 2). None of these is listed as a UC drug in this record.

CXCR2 has no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so MR is not tested (absence of evidence, not evidence against). The mouse literature check shows many colitis papers including a selective CXCR2 antagonist that ameliorated acute colitis, but MGI has no curated colitis phenotype. No safety events are curated and the gene is not strongly constrained.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in UC biopsies, yet plasma MR says genetically higher protein LOWERS UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]), colocalising with the IBD GWAS and replicating in FinnGen (OR [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; finngen_odds_ratio_per_sd=0.734]). The upregulation therefore looks protective/compensatory, and inhibiting PD-L1 (approved checkpoint antibodies exist) would be the wrong direction for UC.

Sensitivity check for CD274 is mixed: only three instruments, Cochran heterogeneity p [gene=CD274; type=mr_sensitivity; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; layer=plasma_protein; heterogeneity_p=0.0259], Steiger direction correct, no colon or gut-cell eQTL instrument. No safety events curated; LOEUF indicates it is not strongly constrained.

IL12B is the known-target positive control: top Open Targets UC association, and plasma MR shows higher protein raises UC risk (OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]), colocalising with IBD GWAS and replicating in FinnGen; inhibition is the protective direction, matching the approved p40-blocking drug class.

Safety/sensitivity for IL12B: not strongly constrained, no curated safety events; the genetic signal is shared with psoriasis, vasculitis and mouth ulcers, and the MR instruments show significant heterogeneity, although MR-Egger intercept is non-significant and Steiger direction is correct.

CXCL5 is strongly up in biopsies but plasma MR says higher protein lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634]), replicating in FinnGen but without IBD GWAS colocalisation and with a tag variant; blocking this chemokine could therefore be the wrong direction.

CXCL8 is a top expression-led biomarker/target (meta-analysis, same direction in all eight cohorts, anti-CXCL8 antibodies ABX-IL8 and adakitug at Phase 2) but has no genetic support: no Open Targets genetic association and plasma MR not significant (p [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]), not replicated in FinnGen. Mouse papers exist but give no curated direction.

IDO1 is strongly up and has drugs (epacadostat, linrodostat) but no human genetic support: plasma MR is null (p [gene=IDO1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.111]) and colon-tissue eQTL MR is also not significant. Likely an inflammation-response marker rather than a causal target.

SLC26A3 has OT genetic association, and gut cell-type eQTL MR in OLFM4+ crypt progenitors gives an odds ratio above one for genetically higher expression (OR per SD [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607]), colocalising and replicating in FinnGen. This direction conflicts with the loss of SLC26A3 in inflamed biopsies (see the expression stream), so the biopsy loss is likely a consequence of inflammation; no drug exists, and the estimate rests on one instrument in one cell type.

FCGR2A has a high Open Targets association and is up in biopsies, but plasma MR is null (p [gene=FCGR2A; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.68]); FinnGen and the Liu 2023 GWAS nominally favour a protective direction, and the gut cell eQTL is also not significant. No drug is listed.

JAK2 is a genetically supported known target (second in the Open Targets UC list) but only modestly changed in biopsies (low expression component), so it is a genetics-led rather than expression-led candidate.

MMP1 (and the MMP3, MMP7, MMP10 family) is strongly up and replicated across cohorts, with only broad MMP inhibitors (marimastat, doxycycline) and no Open Targets genetic association, so these are tissue-damage biomarkers rather than genetically supported targets.

Gut eQTL MR points to genetically driven IRF5 and IRF8 expression in colon (GTEx transverse colon) raising UC risk with IBD GWAS colocalisation, as genetically supported but non-biopsy-led candidates.

caveats: Plasma protein is not mucosal protein; most candidates had no gut eQTL instrument and CXCR2 had no instrument at all (not tested is not evidence against).
MR for several hits uses one to three instruments or tag variants; CD274 and IL12B show heterogeneity.
MGI has no curated colitis phenotype for the genes checked; the mouse literature check only shows the gene was tested, not the result.
Drug lists come from Open Targets and may be in non-UC indications.
